newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU panel still divided over stability pact - sources.
newsitem.headline: EU panel still divided over stability pact - sources.

text.p: The European Union's monetary committee failed early on Wednesday, after 16 hours of talks, to reach an accord on a budget stability pact for countries joining a common currency, EU sources said.
"I think they will present something in Dublin that looks okay," said one source in reference to a summit of EU leaders in Dublin on December 13 and 14. "But it won't be the final version."
The sources said the committee remained at odds over how to quantify the exceptional economic circumstances that would allow a government inside monetary union to avoid sanctions.
Under the proposed plan, countries running annual deficits above three percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) could face stiff fines if they failed to curb expenditure.
Germany, the catalyst behind the so-called stability pact, remained firmly against what it perceives as a watering-down of its initial proposal.
Juergen Stark, German state secretary for finance, was said to still back a proposal that includes a two percent annual decline in output as a necessary condition for a country to avoid fines.
